text.p: Belgian holding company Almanij said on Wednesday 1997 would be a "very satisfactory" year and added that it viewed the coming years with confidence.

Chairman Jan Huyghebaert said in a speech to shareholders, "(1997) will again be very satisfactory...the group companies had a brilliant 1996, driven by a favourable interest rate structure and active markets to which they reacted skillfully and imaginatively at home and abroad."
The companies also applied strict cost management.
"More than ever in view of the continuing good results of our group companies we face the coming years with confidence."
Group net profit rose to 7.1 billion francs in 1996 from 6.1 billion in 1995, Almanij said in April.

Late last month Almanij was at the centre of a major reshuffle involving fellow holding companies Gevaert and Cobepa. Almanij, Cobepa and Gevaert moved to simplify their structures to try and cut the discount at which their shares trade on the stock market.
Gevaert's portfolio was split between Almanij and Cobepa.

The deal strengthened Almanij's capital base and was seen helping it support Belgian bank Kredietbank, a key asset. Kredietbank confirmed last month it was holding exploratory talks with Dutch co-operative bank Rabobank.
